summary: Extend the citation to cover both halves of the quotation
rationale: Verse 63/38 contains u maqṣadayḏan kule i taǧara yo; 63/39 continues with d mšarkat aʕmayna. The glossary example combines these consecutive verses, so replacing 39 with 38 alone would still omit part of the quotation.

data.turoyo: Mənayye kəmšarki, mənayye kul ʕayle l ruḥa kšəmṭo, kmaləmile, ksaymile kawmoṯo.
data.translation: Manche tun sich zusammen, und bei anderen reißt jede Familie für sich (das Gras) aus. Sie sammeln es und häufen es auf.

rationale: Thin II.1 Infectum cell; objectless cooperative work contrasts with each family separately, extending partnership beyond trade.

after: beteiligen; (mit ʕam) sich beteiligen, sich zusammentun
rationale: The inherited Imperativ admits another participant, but inherited 63/39 joins existing associates and JTM 1.1/67 describes families working together without an object. Clarifies both directions of the partnership meaning, rather than treating all uses as transitive beteiligen.

summary: II has an active transitive admission request with -li and objectless participation, optionally with ʕam associates. Objectless cooperation is not Detransitive.
Agricultural collective work broadens the setting of the inherited trade partnership without changing the lexical meaning. The Arabic borrowing is lexical, not a light-verb idiom.
Verify whether ʕam is required for an explicitly named associate or optional when partners are recoverable, as in JTM 1.1/67.
Collective grass-gathering rather than commerce; same partnership meaning and participant grouping.
